"Prediction intervals for alloys from unseen families: family-calibrated conformal prediction for machine-learned alloy properties"
for consideration as a Full-Length Article in the
Journal of Materials Research and Technology

Machine-learning models are now routinely used to screen alloys, including high-entropy and other multi-principal-element alloys, before synthesis. The alloys of greatest interest usually belong to chemical systems or composition regions that are absent from the training data, yet the uncertainty estimates attached to these predictions are calibrated and validated on randomly held-out alloys. Our manuscript quantifies what this costs and proposes a remedy.

Across six public datasets (MPEA hardness and yield strength, steel yield strength, and three inorganic-compound properties), nominal 90% conformal prediction intervals calibrated on random splits covered only 72–87% of alloys from unseen alloy families. We introduce family-calibrated conformal prediction (FCP), which calibrates on whole held-out alloy families with a leakage-free, novelty-aware scale. FCP restored mean coverage to 0.92 (unseen chemical systems) and 0.90 (unseen composition clusters). In a lower-bound screening task for high-performing alloys it reduced false discoveries from 4.6% to 1.2%. The paper reports the costs and limits openly. Intervals are wider; a random-forest heuristic is a strong uncalibrated competitor; and alloy families with extreme properties, such as maraging-type steels and refractory MPEAs, remain the hardest cases.

We believe the work fits the journal's scope because it addresses the reliability of data-driven alloy design, a topic the journal publishes regularly, and provides metallurgically interpretable guidance on when ML-based property predictions for new alloy systems can be trusted. All data are public, and every number, table and figure is regenerated by the supplied code with a single command.

We confirm that this manuscript is original, has not been published previously, and is not under consideration for publication elsewhere. All authors have approved the manuscript and agree with its submission. The study uses only publicly available materials data and involves no human or animal subjects. The authors declare no competing interests. The use of an AI assistant during code development, analysis and drafting is declared in the manuscript in accordance with Elsevier policy.
Thank you for considering our submission.
